source.title: Time-Scale Coupling Between States and Parameters in Recurrent Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies gated recurrent networks and gradient propagation, but does not test the claim versions about classification error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training MSE reductions on regression tasks, not classification error on CIFAR or the conditions named in the claim versions. Those results are recorded as findings about gradient-based training outside the listed versions. Its effective-learning-rate and anisotropy measurements do not measure the claim's stated outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures recurrent gradient transport, update anisotropy and online regression MSE. It does not compare initializations, network depths, teacher/student widths, batch normalization, or learning rates relative to a stability threshold, and does not measure CIFAR classification training error. Its proposed extensions to feedforward networks are future directions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that recurrent gates couple state time scales to parameter dynamics, shaping lag-dependent effective learning rates and directional gradient structure. Their simulations support this mechanism; they do not test any of V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use recurrent networks on synthetic sequence regression tasks and a psMNIST regression surrogate, measuring gradient propagation, update geometry, and training MSE rather than classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports task-dependent training-loss reductions and lag-profile differences across leaky, scalar-gated, and multi-gated RNNs; update anisotropy also varies by task and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Online regression MSE decreases across the tested recurrent architecture/optimizer pairs, with task-dependent reductions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reported recurrent training recipes reduce online regression MSE over 1200 updates on the tested tasks; AR(2) serves as a control with target-independent inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Gating changes lag-dependent sensitivities and produces more concentrated gradient-covariance spectra than plain RNNs trained with Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent gating shapes temporal gradient transport and parameter-gradient geometry under the tested sequence-regression protocols.

record.problems: The training-loss reductions are reported as aggregate ranges or values across architecture+optimizer pairs rather than as separate exact values for each pair. The paper describes these as regression-task diagnostics, not classification performance.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for gradient norms, lag-dependent effective-learning-rate slopes, or anisotropy metrics: they do not measure the training-error outcome named in the claim versions. The study reports further task- and architecture-specific geometry results in Sections VII and VIII-G, Figures 3–10 and Table III.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, random or corrupted labels, model-size effects, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima and additional student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity residual shortcuts and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, learning speed, trainable depth and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Stability-threshold learning-rate comparisons, catapult recovery, divergence and sharpness trajectories.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, despite clear MSE reductions. Finite gradient norms and decreasing loss at fixed learning rates do not establish stability-threshold recovery. The omitted geometry results are declared in rows_left_out and bear on none of the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, label corruption, model size, and early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth effects on classification training error, and the named special cases.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on feedforward or convolutional network training.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness trajectories.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks.
